features.method: Midpoint (6142 m from the Assergi portal) of the LNGS laboratory access zone, itself walked along the OSM tunnel line from the official emergency-plan chainage of the laboratory's entrance and exit doors (see that record's method). This is the best-sourced position for the LNGS underground complex as a whole; no source consulted (checked 2026-09-18) distinguishes which position within the roughly 700 m access zone this hall occupies, or the order of Halls A, B and C along it, so all three hall records are drawn at this same point and accuracy is widened to 400 m (roughly the zone's own half-span) to say so.

features.method: Walked along geometry:lngs-tunnel-gran-sasso's line from its Assergi (west) end, cumulatively (haversine, 45 vertices): 5787 m (the laboratory's exit doors) to 6497 m (its entrance doors). The two distances come from the official emergency plan's A24 motorway chainage: the tunnel bore runs km 117.653 (Assergi portal) to km 127.829 (Teramo portal); the laboratory's own doors are stated at km 124.150 (entrance) and km 123.440 (exit); subtracting the portal chainage (117.653 km) from each gives the distance-from-Assergi-portal used here. Both target distances fell on the same original OSM segment, so the drawn line is a straight 2-point sub-segment of the tunnel line, not a freehand shape.
features.name: LNGS underground laboratory access zone (Gran Sasso tunnel, km 123.440-124.150)

provenance.locator: src:geo-lngs-pee-2024 p.27-28 (chainage); walked along geometry:lngs-tunnel-gran-sasso's own OSM line
provenance.note: The straight-line distance between the two endpoints below (710.0 m by haversine) matches the official chainage delta (124.150 - 123.440 = 0.710 km) to within 4 m, which corroborates that A24 motorway chainage and this OSM way's own cumulative length correspond closely over this stretch (the whole-tunnel length check on geometry:lngs-tunnel-gran-sasso passes at 0.10%). A different part of the same source states the door-to-door distance is 'ca. 500 m' rather than the 710 m implied by its own two km markers; both figures are reported here rather than silently reconciled.

features.method: OpenStreetMap relation 9617984, member way 24389234 (the Assergi/west-portal-first tube), taken verbatim as one LineString. The relation's other member (way 362100840, the twin parallel bore) is not drawn separately: the two tubes run 30-90 m apart (average ca. 60 m per src:geo-lngs-pee-2024) and drawing both at this map's scale would be a near-duplicate shape with no added information; the single drawn tube stands for the tunnel's path.
